# zlags2

> Computes 2-by-2 unitary matrices U, V, and Q for the generalized upper (lower) triangular form.

<section class="usage">

## Usage

```js
import zlags2 from '@rreusser/blahpack/lapack/zlags2';
```

### Layout API

Takes a storage layout (`order`) and leading dimensions, like CBLAS/LAPACKE.

```js
zlags2( upper, a1, a2, a3, b1, b2, b3, csu, snu, csv, snv, csq, snq ) → void
```

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `upper` | `boolean` | Whether the input matrices are upper triangular |
| `a1` | `number` | (1,1) element of A (real) |
| `a2` | `Complex128` | Off-diagonal element of A (complex) |
| `a3` | `number` | (2,2) element of A (real) |
| `b1` | `number` | (1,1) element of B (real) |
| `b2` | `Complex128` | Off-diagonal element of B (complex) |
| `b3` | `number` | (2,2) element of B (real) |
| `csu` | `Float64Array` | **out** · Output (length-1 array): `csu` |
| `snu` | `Complex128Array` | **out** · Output (length-1 array): the desired unitary matrix U |
| `csv` | `Float64Array` | **out** · Output (length-1 array): `csv` |
| `snv` | `Complex128Array` | **out** · Output (length-1 array): the desired unitary matrix V |
| `csq` | `Float64Array` | **out** · Output (length-1 array): `csq` |
| `snq` | `Complex128Array` | **out** · Output (length-1 array): the desired unitary matrix Q |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `upper`: = .TRUE.: the input matrices A and B are upper triangular. = .FALSE.: the input matrices A and B are lower triangular.
- `a3`: On entry, `A1`, `A2` and `A3` are elements of the input 2-by-2 upper (lower) triangular matrix A.
- `b3`: On entry, `B1`, `B2` and `B3` are elements of the input 2-by-2 upper (lower) triangular matrix B.
- `snu`: The desired unitary matrix U.
- `snv`: The desired unitary matrix V.
- `snq`: The desired unitary matrix Q.

</details>

**Returns** `void`

### Strided (ndarray) API

Takes explicit strides and offsets for every array. Use it for views, sub-matrices and non-unit strides.

```js
zlags2.ndarray(
    upper, a1, a2, a3, b1, b2, b3,
    csu,
    snu, offsetSnu,
    csv,
    snv, offsetSnv,
    csq,
    snq, offsetSnq
) → void
```

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `upper` | `boolean` | Whether the input matrices are upper triangular |
| `a1` | `number` | (1,1) element of A (real) |
| `a2` | `Complex128` | Off-diagonal element of A (complex) |
| `a3` | `number` | (2,2) element of A (real) |
| `b1` | `number` | (1,1) element of B (real) |
| `b2` | `Complex128` | Off-diagonal element of B (complex) |
| `b3` | `number` | (2,2) element of B (real) |
| `csu` | `Float64Array` | **out** · Output (length-1 array): `csu` |
| `snu` | `Complex128Array` | **out** · Output (length-1 array): the desired unitary matrix U |
| ↳ `offsetSnu` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for `snu` (in complex elements) |
| `csv` | `Float64Array` | **out** · Output (length-1 array): `csv` |
| `snv` | `Complex128Array` | **out** · Output (length-1 array): the desired unitary matrix V |
| ↳ `offsetSnv` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for `snv` (in complex elements) |
| `csq` | `Float64Array` | **out** · Output (length-1 array): `csq` |
| `snq` | `Complex128Array` | **out** · Output (length-1 array): the desired unitary matrix Q |
| ↳ `offsetSnq` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for `snq` (in complex elements) |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `upper`: = .TRUE.: the input matrices A and B are upper triangular. = .FALSE.: the input matrices A and B are lower triangular.
- `a3`: On entry, `A1`, `A2` and `A3` are elements of the input 2-by-2 upper (lower) triangular matrix A.
- `b3`: On entry, `B1`, `B2` and `B3` are elements of the input 2-by-2 upper (lower) triangular matrix B.
- `snu`: The desired unitary matrix U.
- `snv`: The desired unitary matrix V.
- `snq`: The desired unitary matrix Q.

</details>

**Returns** `void`

</section>

## Notes

-   `zlags2()` corresponds to the reference LAPACK routine [`ZLAGS2`](https://github.com/Reference-LAPACK/lapack/blob/v3.12.0/SRC/zlags2.f).

<section class="examples">

## Examples

```js
import Complex128 from '@stdlib/complex/float64/ctor/lib/index.js';
import zlags2 from '@rreusser/blahpack/lapack/zlags2';
import Complex128Array from '@stdlib/array/complex128/lib/index.js';
import reinterpret from '@stdlib/strided/base/reinterpret-complex128/lib/index.js';

const csu = new Float64Array( 1 );
const snu = new Complex128Array( 1 );
const snuv = reinterpret( snu, 0 );
const csv = new Float64Array( 1 );
const snv = new Complex128Array( 1 );
const snvv = reinterpret( snv, 0 );
const csq = new Float64Array( 1 );
const snq = new Complex128Array( 1 );
const snqv = reinterpret( snq, 0 );

zlags2( true, 4.0, new Complex128( 2.0, 1.0 ), 3.0, 1.0, new Complex128( 0.5, 0.25 ), 2.0, csu, snu, csv, snv, csq, snq );
const out = {
	'csu': csu[ 0 ],
	'snuR': snuv[ 0 ],
	'snuI': snuv[ 1 ],
	'csv': csv[ 0 ],
	'snvR': snvv[ 0 ],
	'snvI': snvv[ 1 ],
	'csq': csq[ 0 ],
	'snqR': snqv[ 0 ],
	'snqI': snqv[ 1 ]
}; // eslint-disable-line max-len
console.log( out ); // eslint-disable-line no-console
```

</section>

<!-- /.examples -->

<section class="reference-notes">

## Reference notes

The mathematical description from the reference LAPACK 3.12.0 source of `ZLAGS2`. Indices are the 1-based Fortran indices of the source.

### Purpose

ZLAGS2 computes 2-by-2 unitary matrices U, V and Q, such that if ( `UPPER` ) then

```text
          U**H *A*Q = U**H *( A1 A2 )*Q = ( x  0  )
                            ( 0  A3 )     ( x  x  )
and
          V**H*B*Q = V**H *( B1 B2 )*Q = ( x  0  )
                           ( 0  B3 )     ( x  x  )
```

or if ( .NOT.`UPPER` ) then

```text
          U**H *A*Q = U**H *( A1 0  )*Q = ( x  x  )
                            ( A2 A3 )     ( 0  x  )
and
          V**H *B*Q = V**H *( B1 0  )*Q = ( x  x  )
                            ( B2 B3 )     ( 0  x  )
```

where

$$
U = \begin{pmatrix} \mathrm{CSU} & \mathrm{SNU} \\ -\mathrm{SNU}^H & \mathrm{CSU} \end{pmatrix} , V = \begin{pmatrix} \mathrm{CSV} & \mathrm{SNV} \\ -\mathrm{SNV}^H & \mathrm{CSV} \end{pmatrix}
$$

$$
Q = \begin{pmatrix} \mathrm{CSQ} & \mathrm{SNQ} \\ -\mathrm{SNQ}^H & \mathrm{CSQ} \end{pmatrix}
$$

The rows of the transformed A and B are parallel. Moreover, if the input 2-by-2 matrix A is not zero, then the transformed (1,1) entry of A is not zero. If the input matrices A and B are both not zero, then the transformed (2,2) element of B is not zero, except when the first rows of input A and B are parallel and the second rows are zero.

</section>
